Hi Frank — looping in with initial findings after a quick pass on the export.

We pulled a condensed export for your billing window (attached: acme-raw-export-sample.csv and redwood-partial-log-sample-20261107.jsonl). The sampled data (first 72 hours of the spike window) shows three clear patterns:

- Client-side retries: ~38% of duplicate accepted requests have identical client_request_id and timestamps separated by <2s.
- Upstream queue replay: ~12% look like transient router replays — same request_id but delivered twice to the runtime due to a narrow routing flap caught by our queueing layer.
- Legitimate increased usage: the remainder correlates with a marketing batch send you confirmed on Oct 28.

Numbers (sample window):
- Normal accepted request baseline: ~76k/day
- Spike window accepted requests: ~183k/day
- Estimated duplicates (sample): ~34k requests 
- Estimated bill impact (sample extrapolated): $3,420 (before VAT)

Proposed next steps:
1) We can run a full export for the full invoice period (this will take up to 24 hours).
2) If Redwood-origin duplicates (router replays) account for >=5% of billed units across the full window, we will issue a one-time credit for the attributable amount.
3) For client-origin retries, we will provide the list of client_request_ids and timestamps so Acme can correlate with your server logs; we can also recommend idempotency headers to avoid this pattern.

As a show of good faith and because the sampled data shows some router replays, I'm proposing a provisional credit of $1,874.25 pending the full export. That credit would be applied as a negative line on your next invoice and accompanied by an itemized credit note. Please confirm if that approach works for Acme (we'll then produce the full export and the official credit note).

Attachments: acme-raw-export-sample.csv (text/csv, 55KB), redwood-partial-log-sample-20261107.jsonl (application/jsonl, 120KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
